messages:
sophie_cs: Quick intake from Orion (customer). They see search results suddenly misaligned after our 2.0 model rollout — embeddings no longer match indexes; they claim embedding IDs shifted causing wrong docs returned. They've provided repro steps and sample payloads. Marking P2 for now, customer impact = sporadic incorrect search hits (non-security).

maria_support: Adding the reproduction steps they gave below. They say it happens ~10% of queries, mostly on multi-shard embed indexes.

sophie_cs: Repro steps (copied verbatim from customer):
1) Create 3k embedding vectors with our embeddings endpoint using model redwood-embed-1.
2) Index using their vector DB (open-source indexer) with embedding IDs from our response order.
3) After deploying our 2.0 text-gen+embed rollout, running same queries returns different top-k docs.
4) They re-fetched embeddings for a random 50 ids and observed that embedding bytes for some ids differ from the original upload by ~1-2 bits (not just scale).

sophie_cs: They included a short curl to reproduce the embed call we used:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3"]}'
```

sophie_cs: And a small binary diff from their side (base64 snippets):
```
orig: AAABBBCC... (truncated)
new:  AAABBDCC... (bit flip near offset 438)
```

josh_eng: Thanks, Sophie. A couple quick q's: 1) Are they using Dedicated or Hosted? 2) Any signs of retry/re-ordering on our side (client replays)?

maria_support: Customer on Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), region eu-west-1. They said no client-side retries. They ported exactly the ID mapping we returned at upload time.

josh_eng: Ok. That narrows things. My immediate suspicion: KV-cache rotation / memory reuse bug in the embed pipeline where buffer contents aren't zeroed on reuse — causing rare bit corruption across sequences. Could also be a serialization/quantization mismatch across the 2.0 rollout (different kernel path).

amar_engineer: On Dedicated we did flip to the new low-precision packing kernels last week for embeds. We also changed the temp buffer pooling for perf. I'll try to repro locally by replaying their payloads + stress test.

sophie_cs: Customer supplied a small repro dataset and a reproducible script. They've consented for us to run it in their dedicated pool (they gave access token scope limited). Uploading the script to internal S3.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of embed runtime (rp-embeds-v2) finished at 2134509000, canary nodes=3/3, health=pass.

josh_eng: Amar, if you can repro on canary nodes that'd be huge. Steps for eng triage:
- Run the exact customer script against a canary node with the same model + kernel flags.
- Capture raw byte outputs for embeddings (base64) and compare with previous stable runtime.
- If mismatch, dump process memory of embed buffers around that request and grep for reused pointer addresses.
- Link findings here and open a bug in GH with label "customer-impact" and "dedicated".

sara_pm: From product: flagging as potential roadmap impact. If this is caused by kernel switch we need a roadmap slot to validate embed kernel parity across deployment modes and add a canary gating checklist. Acceptance criteria suggestion:
- Repro/test harness added to CI that verifies deterministic embedding outputs for a canonical corpus across runtime versions.
- Rollback/mitigation playbook documented for Dedicated customers.

sophie_cs: Customer wants a timeline and whether we can revert the embed kernel change for them specifically. They asked for an ETA within 48h.

josh_eng: Prioritize triage now. Amar, can you confirm whether we can toggle kernel packing per-tenant? If not, fallback option would be a quick rollback of rp-embeds-v2 to stable on their pool. That depends on infra lead.

amar_engineer: I'll start running repros now on canary. If I hit reproducible corruption I'll attach heap dumps. If the issue looks like buffer reuse, it should be patchable without model changes. I can probably have an initial triage by EOD (within ~8 hours).

sara_pm: Good. If triage confirms kernel cause, I'll schedule a short roadmap conversation with infra and eng-runtime to scope the mitigation and customer opt-out/backfill plan.

maria_support: Logging note: Customer name: Orion Labs (org id: orion-9021). Impact: production search mismatch in Dedicated eu-west-1. SLA tier: enterprise. Customer is on-call and sensitive to data integrity.

sophie_cs: Next actions (agreed):
- Amar: reproduce & post findings (by EOD).
- Josh: prep GH bug template and label.
- Sara: hold a 30-min sync tomorrow if root cause confirmed.
- Maria: keep customer updated (we promised regular 6-8h status updates).

josh_eng: I'll create the GH issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/5678 (placeholder). Adding labels: bug, customer-impact, dedicated, embeds.

amar_engineer: Update: initial run on canary shows one mismatch after ~1200 embeds; capturing heap and payloads now. Dumping into /tmp/orion-repro-213450. Will attach to GH issue.

sophie_cs: Thanks everyone. Maria, pls send the next update to Orion saying we're triaging and will revert kernel if needed; include the canary deploy timestamp.

maria_support: Sent update at 2134511200: "We are investigating with eng. You will get an update within 8 hours." Customer replied with acknowledgement :thumbsup:.

sophie_cs: Closing intake here; will update thread when GH issue has root-cause and mitigation plan.
